sd67Remediation.closes: SD-6 (unattested commitment install on rotation and recovery) and SD-7 (genesis admits a commitment its own declared floor cannot satisfy)
sd67Remediation.abiChange: TWO ENTRIES, both intended, nothing else. initialize(GenesisConfig) -> initialize(GenesisConfig,bytes) and deployVault(bytes32,GenesisConfig) -> deployVault(bytes32,GenesisConfig,bytes). Selector counts unchanged at 45 and 4. genesisSalt and predictVault are UNTOUCHED, so the CONFIGURATION -> SALT function is unchanged; Sd67AdmissionInvariants.test.ts pins genesisSalt for a canonical configuration against a constant captured from the parent build. THAT PINS THE SALT, NOT AN ADDRESS: a clone's address is CREATE2(factory, salt, keccak256(initcode)) and the ERC-1167 initcode embeds the IMPLEMENTATION address, so every deployed address moves whenever the kernel bytecode moves — true of every remediation in this stack, and not something any change to this kernel could avoid.
sd67Remediation.whyTheWitnessIsNotInGenesisConfig: genesisSalt binds the genesis AUTHORITY and a preimage proof confers none. Putting the witness inside the struct would additionally change predictVault's ABI and would invite a later editor to add it to the salt enumeration, which WOULD change the configuration -> salt map. The ledger's recorded reason for deferring this fix — that a new struct member changes every vault address BECAUSE the struct is hashed into the salt — is false in its MECHANISM: genesisSalt hashes an enumerated field list, not the struct as a unit, so a new member alone moves no salt. Addresses do move, but for a reason that applies to every change in this stack (the clone initcode embeds the implementation address), so it never distinguished this fix from any other.
sd67Remediation.note: The dormant clause deliberately omits any LENGTH comparison. While requirePq is false the floor lengths are unvalidated (_requireSaneFloor returns early) and unfrozen (_requireNoDowngrade is guarded on the current floor), so reading them at install time would let one cut-1 setVerifier make executeRecovery undeliverable forever. Residual SD-8: an exhibit proves a preimage, never that the preimage is a well-formed key of any scheme, and no admission check can establish that without a verifier the admitting principal chooses.
sd67Remediation._hashNote: Both sha256 values were re-measured from a CLEAN rebuild AFTER the final comment and NatSpec edits. solc hashes every source in the compilation unit into the metadata CBOR, so a comment-only edit moves the hash while leaving the byte COUNT identical — 18,105 and 2,445 both before and after those edits.
